title: The Limits of AI as an Economic Weapon
gist: Bessler argues AI is heading toward a divided market, with a large commoditized tier of Chinese open-weight models and a small premium tier of closed US frontier models, which undermines AI models as a US chokepoint. Real US leverage remains in chips and in cloud hosting and inference, where he recommends narrow chip controls and keeping clouds American.

insights.claim: AI demand will likely split like pharmaceuticals into a large commoditized pool of cheap models and a smaller premium tier of frontier offerings, weakening the inventing state's power.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Expect margin pressure on frontier-model pricing for routine tasks, with premium value concentrated in complex use cases.

insights.claim: In US pharmaceuticals, generics are 90% of prescriptions but 12% of spending, while brands are 10% of prescriptions and 88% of spending, which is the analogy for the AI split.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: The volume/profit split gives a template for where AI profits will concentrate.

insights.claim: Vercel's September 2026 report said open-weight models processed 56% of August's gateway tokens but accounted for only 14% of spend.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Direct evidence of the volume/value split; track gateway data as a share-shift indicator.
insights.quote: Open-weight models processed 56% of August’s gateway tokens and accounted for 14% of spend.
insights.locator: A Dividing AI Market on the Horizon

insights.claim: A July CNBC report found that the share of tokens US companies use on Chinese models via OpenRouter has sat above 30% since February and reached as high as 46%.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: US enterprises are already routing heavily to Chinese open models, despite quiet disclosure.
insights.locator: A Dividing AI Market on the Horizon

insights.claim: Chinese open models still trail the American frontier on benchmarks like Epoch and METR, but a divided market only requires the commodity tier to be good enough on cost.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Capability gaps matter less than price for routine workloads; do not assume frontier lead protects revenue.
insights.locator: A Dividing AI Market on the Horizon

insights.claim: Firms have incentives to stay quiet about using Chinese models, so usage measurement is understated, and OpenAI's API alone moves about six and a half times as many tokens monthly as all OpenRouter models combined.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Gateway share data is a partial, biased gauge; treat headline percentages with caution.
insights.locator: A Dividing AI Market on the Horizon

insights.claim: Hugging Face found the majority of its 2025 trending models were either developed in China or derivative of a China-developed model.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Chinese dominance of the open-weight ecosystem is already visible in download trends.
insights.locator: A Dividing AI Market on the Horizon

insights.claim: A flood of Chinese open models could starve US frontier labs of the profits they rely on to fund the best models for the military, a concern raised by Daniel Francis.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Frontier lab economics are tied to national security argument; expect lobbying for government support.
insights.locator: A Dividing AI Market on the Horizon

themes.theme: AI as an economic weapon and chokepoints

insights.claim: Washington has repeatedly gained coercive leverage from US tech firms abroad, such as cutting Huawei off from Android in 2019 and TSMC chips in 2020, after which Huawei's global smartphone share fell from 20% in 2020 to virtually nothing outside mainland China by 2024.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Precedent for tech sanctions; shows what an effective chokepoint looks like.

insights.claim: Edward Fishman's three chokepoint conditions are dominant concentrated share, no short-term substitutes, and the ability to impose asymmetric pain with minimal self-harm.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Use as a checklist to test whether any technology layer provides real sanctions leverage.
insights.quote: a single country or coalition of close allies possesses a dominant, concentrated market share

insights.claim: A divided AI market denies Washington an AI-model chokepoint because free, improving substitutes exist, and sanctioning Chinese models could backfire by spurring open-source development elsewhere.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Model-layer sanctions are unlikely to be effective; lower odds of broad bans on Chinese open models.

insights.claim: Restricting Chinese open models would disrupt thrifty US firms and push allies to build their own sovereign models, probably based on Chinese open weights run locally.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Policy risk is skewed toward non-restriction; allies' sovereign AI efforts may use Chinese weights.

insights.claim: US frontier labs are locked into profit-driven strategies with little incentive to build top-rate open-weight models, so China will likely dominate the open-weight sector for the foreseeable future.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Open-weight leadership will likely stay Chinese; US response limited by lab economics.

insights.claim: Francis's proposal to subsidize labs to reserve their best models for government fails to preserve a chokepoint, because a model that never diffuses leaves Washington no lever.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Locking down frontier models trades economic leverage for military use.
insights.quote: A model that never diffuses is no chokepoint

insights.claim: Nvidia and non-frontier US firms benefit from cheap Chinese open-weight models because they drive demand for domestic data centers and let startups automate tasks too costly on Claude or GPT.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Compute and application-layer firms benefit from model commoditization; frontier labs bear the margin risk.

insights.claim: After Anthropic accused Chinese labs in July of distilling Claude into open-weight models, Nvidia led more than 270 tech companies in an open letter against restricting Chinese open-weight models; OpenAI and Google signed late and Anthropic has not signed.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Industry split on open-weight restrictions shows divergent interests between chips and frontier labs.

themes.theme: Lessons of Japan's DRAM and remaining US levers

insights.claim: Japan took 80% of global DRAM by 1987 yet gained no coercive power, because DRAM had too many manufacturers and easy substitutes, and US firms recovered by moving up the value chain to PCs, microprocessors and networking.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Analogy suggests value accrues to layers built on commoditized inputs, not the commodity layer itself.

insights.claim: AI compute passes the chokepoint test: about 39.7 million petaflops of AI compute are in the US versus roughly 400,000 in China, and Nvidia holds over 85% of AI chip share.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Chip export controls remain the strongest US lever; Nvidia's position is a core strategic asset.

insights.claim: Export controls work on chips because they are narrow; selling too little abroad spurs indigenization while selling too much speeds China toward the frontier.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Chip policy calibration affects both Nvidia revenue and China's pace.

insights.claim: A second chokepoint is AI hosting and inference: US clouds hold over 70% of the market, Moonshot is negotiating to put Kimi K3 on all three largest, and Thomson Reuters and Harvey have built on Qwen and Kimi K3.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Hyperscalers capture value from hosting cheap Chinese models; application firms hold the customer relationship.

insights.claim: Bessler recommends Washington keep chip controls narrow and keep the clouds American, since the US may lose the ability to dictate which model is used but can own where it runs.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Favors US hyperscalers and Nvidia over model-only labs in a policy-regime view.
insights.quote: Maybe the U.S. can no longer tell you what model to use, but it can own where that model runs.

insights.claim: Moonshot and Alibaba may struggle to profit even as their models do the work, because customers of Harvey and Thomson Reuters pay those application companies directly.
insights.speaker: Max Bessler
insights.so_what: Profits migrate to the application layer, not to open-model developers.
